hypothesis: Stopping automatic recovery after one preserved-work continuation exhausts active runtime will prevent repeated six-hour builder loops while keeping every change available to the typed state-recovery review surface.

metricsCompared.name: automatic active-runtime continuations per preserved worktree
metricsCompared.baseline: An exhausted continuation was explicitly eligible to emit another recovery request.
metricsCompared.candidate: The first exhausted continuation records state-recovery-required and emits no recovery request; recovery scans honor recoveryRequested=false.

metricsCompared.name: preserved-work observability
metricsCompared.baseline: A terminal artifact only exposed recoveryRequested and generic cleanup blockers.
metricsCompared.candidate: The terminal artifact contains a typed recovery action with inspect and resolve commands.

rationale: The candidate changes only the repeated active-timeout path. Original failed work remains preserved until an explicit state-recovery disposition, while classified provider failures retain their existing retry behavior. Focused tests prove both no re-emission and no later recovery-scan requeue.
